title: Postmortem: unexpected rapid scale-down due to metric attenuation bug
creator: Anika Rao
summary: A regression in autoscaling logic caused an aggressive scale-down across a subset of inference pools, producing cold starts and elevated tail latencies for hosted customers over a ~22 minute window. The incident was triggered by a metric transformation change that attenuated recent percentile values fed to KEDA scalers, leading HPAs to undershoot desired replica counts.
impact: Approximately 8% of hosted API requests experienced >2x tail latency and ~3% of production requests returned transient 503s. Two midsize customers on Dedicated experienced request rejections during the event window. No data loss or model corruption occurred. Estimated business impact: brief SLA latency degradation and customer support churn for 3 customers.
detection: Pager alert for API latency and increased 5xx rate triggered at 2026-02-28T10:07Z. On-call escalated to runtime SRE; initial mitigation applied by increasing replica floor via emergency scaling policy at 10:16Z.
timeline: 2026-02-28T09:54Z - Kinesis metric pipeline deployment (internal change) rolled out: 'percentile_normalizer_v2' enabled for rollout group B.
2026-02-28T10:02Z - Gradual increase in 95th token latency observed on prod-batch metric dashboards.
2026-02-28T10:07Z - Automated latency alert fired (P95 > 500ms for 5m). On-call informed and incident declared.
2026-02-28T10:10Z - Investigation identified correlated drop in reported 95th percentile values consumed by KEDA external scaler for several pools.
2026-02-28T10:12Z - Correlation between metric attenuation and KEDA scaler decisions confirmed: scale-downs began shortly after attenuated metrics appeared.
2026-02-28T10:16Z - Emergency manual override: enforced minReplicas increased on impacted HPAs, restoring capacity to expected levels.
2026-02-28T10:24Z - Tail latency and 5xx rates returned to baseline as cold-starts subsided and replica counts stabilized.
2026-02-28T10:36Z - Incident declared resolved; follow-up actions assigned.
2026-03-02T09:00Z - Root cause analysis completed: metric normalizer change introduced a windowing bug for short windows (<=30s) that produced stale/attenuated percentiles under bursty traffic.
2026-03-05T14:00Z - Patch deployed to metric pipeline and KEDA scaler validation checks added; postmortem written and reviewed.
2026-03-05T17:30Z - Runbook updated with explicit warm-pool ramp procedures and emergency HPA override steps.
root_cause: A deployment to the metric normalization service changed the percentile aggregation window semantics (intended to smooth noisy metrics). For small windows under bursty load the algorithm applied an extra decay factor, reducing reported higher-percentile values. KEDA external scalers relied on those attenuated percentiles as their primary input and translated them into lower target replica counts. Combined with insufficient HPA hysteresis and no warm-pool for affected pools, the platform underprovisioned and clients saw cold-starts and surge 503s.
contributing_factors: Metric normalization change introduced without end-to-end integration test against KEDA scalers
KEDA scaler lacked sanity checks for abrupt percentile drops and will accept values without historical consistency validation
HPA configurations for a subset of inference pools had low minReplicas and short stabilization windows (30s), making them sensitive to transient metric changes
No synthetic warm traffic/warm pool for certain latency-sensitive workloads
Insufficient post-deploy monitoring coverage for metric transformation changes (no canary-specific dashboard alerts).
mitigations: Emergency increase of minReplicas for impacted HPAs to enforce capacity floor
Rollback of percentile_normalizer_v2 to previous stable normalization behavior for rollout groups A/B
Manual warm-pool activation for affected instance classes to avoid cold-start penalties
Temporary extension of HPA stabilization window to 3m for burst-prone pools
action_items: ENG-85322: Add end-to-end integration tests that feed normalized percentile metrics into a KEDA test harness (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-19)
ENG-85323: Implement historical-consistency checks in KEDA external scaler logic (reject drops >40% within 60s without confirmation) (owner: Jamal Bennett, due: 2026-03-12)
ENG-85324: Increase default HPA minReplicas for inference pools that serve low-latency SLAs and set stabilization window to 180s (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-85325: Build a lightweight synthetic warm traffic harness and create warm-pool activation runbook (owner: Anika Rao, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-85326: Add canary dashboards and alerts for metric transformation services to detect normalization regressions earlier (owner: Lian Chen, due: 2026-03-10)
ENG-85327: Ship KEDA scaler update to do sanity validation and emit structured events for audit logging (owner: Jamal Bennett, due: 2026-03-18)
ENG-85328: Retro: schedule a cross-team incident review with Observability, Runtime, and SRE to update deployment gating for metric pipeline (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-09)
ENG-85329: Add a unit test in CI that simulates percentile attenuation and verifies HPA decisions do not drop below minReplicas (owner: Mateo Alvarez, due: 2026-03-08)
follow_up_notes: Avoid tight coupling of single-metric normalization services and autoscaler inputs; prefer an adapter layer that applies validation and backpressure
Consider a declarative scaling policy language to encode safety constraints (minReplicas, maxDropPercent, confirmationWindow)
Explore leveraging model-aware warm containers (persisted KV cache) to reduce the cost of warm pools for expensive models
Customer support: notify affected customers with summary of root cause and completed mitigations; offer credit for SLA miss (owner: Customer Success, due: 2026-03-12)
